title: What we know about the typical Polymarket user
excerpt: An analysis of typical user behavior on Polymarket over a six-week period, using the Polymarket API and automated data collection in Python.
content: For this study examining typical user behavior on Polymarket, I used several Polymarket API endpoints in concert with each other to identify a sample of user wallets and track their activity over a six-week period using an automated Python script. The API documentation was sparse at the time of the study and its behavior sometimes contradicted the available documentation, so I cross referenced the API output with publicly available information, such as the Polymarket leaderboards, to confirm correct interpretation of what the API returned. I used this data to show that users mostly place trades on a single topic and tended to make or lose modest amounts of money.

title: Trading volume on prediction markets has soared in recent months
excerpt: An analysis of what's driving the rapidly growing trading volume on the two major prediction markets, Kalshi and Polymarket.
content: Using off-the-shelf data, I found that trading volume on prediction markets had exploded over the course of just a few months, and that sports trading was in large part responsible. I turned this analysis around in just a couple of business days, at an organization that rarely moves at the speed of news. These findings were widely cited in the media, and by government officials looking to rein in what many see as unregulated betting on these sites.

title: Who Are America’s Health and Wellness Influencers?
excerpt: An examination of health and wellness influencer profiles on social media.
content:
I joined this year-long project after it was well underway, but immediately jumped in and made an impact.
— **Codebook development:** manually reviewed posts to determine and refine what we should capture from each profile
— **Programmatically determining where else influencers showed up online:** wrote Python scripts to check for known domains for podcasts and social media sites across a JSON of 7,000 influencers
— **Built analysis tables:** used R and Quarto to analyze the variables we created and organize findings for the whole team to work off of, serving as an initial outline of the report

title: Most new data centers in the U.S. are coming to rural areas
excerpt: An analysis of where current and future data centers will be in the U.S., using a combination of industry and Census data.
content: Using data from an industry database and the Census API, my colleague and I found that most new data centers in the U.S. will be built in more rural areas and more heavily concentrated in the South and Midwest. I took the lead on descriptive statistics and Census analysis of county-level and community-type proximity, while my colleague led our geographic and survey analysis.

title: News Media Tracker
excerpt: A design solution that makes 4 measures across 30 news outlets comprehensible to readers.
content: I worked closely with researchers to devise this design solution that displays both industry-level takeaways and outlet-level details, and is robust to biannual updates that may add or delete individual outlets. Working wtih SEO and UX experts, I also designed pages for each outlet to make the outlet-specific information more easily discoverable.

title: What is News?
excerpt: An illustrated exploration of how news is defined, created, and consumed in the digital age.
content: For this project, I designed all visuals, creating illustrations and charts in Adobe Illustrator and styling quotes and interactive elements in WordPress. I also contributed editorially, helping my research colleagues refine their outline and create a tighter narrative.

title: Why Many Parents and Teens Think It's Harder Being a Teen Today
excerpt: Hand-drawn animated sprites visualizing findings about what parents and teens think about teen life today.
content: In public opinion polling, it is difficult and expensive to survey kids. With this essay exploring what not only parents but also their teens think of teen life today, I wanted to take the opportunity to remind audiences that our findings represent real individuals and their experiences, not just aggregate data points. To do that, I hand-drew and then digitially animated sprites representing teens and parents in a playful, diverse way. I created a static Figma composition of the flow of the essay and other art direction elements to ensure that research colleagues understood and agreed with the concept, and collaborated closely with a web developer to bring to life.

title: Child Labor Violations Increase as States Loosen Rules
excerpt: Original reporting on a rise in reported child labor violations.
content: This story combined reporting, data analysis and visualization to show that child labor violations were on the rise even as many states sought to relax their rules. I analyzed national data from the Department of Labor and interviewed DOL officials and labor activists. Reporting out this story also provided me with the context and knowledge I needed to report on [child labor in the tobacco industry](https://www.npr.org/2023/04/17/1168824035/child-labor-tobacco-legal-dangerous) later on in my NPR internship.

title: What Does the Respect for Marriage Act Do? The Answer Will Vary by State
excerpt: An explainer of the Respect for Marriage Act, with an interactive map.
content: The Respect for Marriage Act had different implications for different states, depending on their existing state-level same-sex marriage laws. Using off-the-shelf data and expert interviews, I put together an explainer to help LGBTQ+ Americans and their families understand the protections offered by this law. I also built an interactive map using Dailygraphics Next and a lookup table using Datawrapper. (Note: NPR's site has undergone updates since this published; tooltips no longer work as intended.)

title: In the Dark: Transparency Rule Fails to Shed Light on Costs for IU Health Bloomington Patients
excerpt: An investigation into hospital price transparency at IU hospitals.
content: This investigation examined whether my local hospital was properly complying with a federal price transparency mandate that sought to make it easier for Americans to predict their hospital bills. In addition to showing how wildly prices varied based on a patient's insurance carrier, the piece explains how patients can negotiate their bills and advocate for themselves under this law.
